paper_title: Stochastic fluctuations of bosonic dark matter
suggested_experiment_name: VULF axion-nucleon laboratory constraints (CASPEr-ZULF / nEDM / New Force)
notes: This is a methodology/theory paper showing that constraints from prior bosonic DM searches (operating in T<<tau_c regime) were overestimated by factors of ~3-10 due to neglecting the stochastic (Rayleigh-distributed) nature of the VULF amplitude. It re-derives correction factors for existing experiments (CASPEr-ZULF, nEDM, dilaton clock searches) rather than presenting a new measured exclusion limit or projection. The modified exclusion plots (axion-nucleon gaNN and dilaton couplings) are corrections of previously published limits, not new data. No new numerical limit table is extractable; coupling types discussed include both axion-nucleon (gaNN) and scalar/dilaton couplings, making a single coupling assignment ambiguous. | Vision: Y-axis is g_aNN in GeV^-1 on log scale (ticks 10^-1 to 10^-9). The black boundary combines CASPEr-ZULF Comagnetometer and nEDM constraints (left region, masses 1e-22 to ~1e-17 eV) and a separate 'New Force / Sidebands' constraint (right region, masses ~1e-16 to 1e-13 eV). Lower boundary traced is the bottom edge of the black exclusion curves. Note units are GeV^-1 (dimension-bearing) though coupling_type AxionNeutron is reported as g_aNN. Values approximate from plot reading. | Calibration: No calibration needed
